comparison: Perfect claim overlap (C3-C11, C55) on dataset description. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes quantitative metrics and data attributes; peer reviewers accepted the dataset composition without challenge, confirming 100+ million trees across 37 sites.

Perfect claim overlap (C25-C30, C64) on height validation. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes RMSE=1.73m with appropriate statistical modeling; peer reviewers accepted 'roughly 2m RMSE' without expressing concerns about methodology or interpretation.

Perfect claim overlap (C37-C40) on canopy-only limitation. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval acknowledges the limitation while noting ecological importance of canopy trees; peer reviewers explicitly accepted this as 'a large step forward from pixel-level data' despite the limitation.

Perfect claim overlap (C43-C44) on visualization tool. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval describes the tool as important for data usability; peer reviewers implicitly accepted it without comment.

Perfect claim overlap (C45-C53) on research motivation. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes logical arguments with citations; peer reviewers strongly endorsed the motivation but wanted more concrete discussion of applications (see second round comments).

Perfect claim overlap (C91-C99) on technical limitations. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval praises transparent discussion of model failures and data quality issues; peer reviewers accepted these acknowledged limitations without challenge.

High overlap (C23-C24, C63) on field validation. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes 69.4% recall with acknowledged methodological limitations; peer reviewers accepted the field validation comparison without challenging methodology or results.

Substantial overlap (C12-C17) on methodology pipeline. OpenEval evaluation is SUPPORTED, praising coherent workflow; peer evaluation is UNCERTAIN, expressing strong surprise that LiDAR was not used for crown segmentation itself, questioning why height wasn't used as fourth dimension despite authors' explanation (C41-C42).

Partial overlap (C41-C42) on LiDAR data fusion. OpenEval evaluation is SUPPORTED, accepting negative experimental results with plausible explanations; peer evaluation is UNCERTAIN, with reviewers expressing surprise about not using LiDAR for segmentation and finding the explanation insufficient.

High overlap (C33-C34, C42) on LiDAR point density. OpenEval evaluation is SUPPORTED, noting context with citations; peer evaluation is UNCERTAIN, requesting clearer justification for why LiDAR could not improve crown detection despite low resolution and inconsistencies.

Overlap (C18-C22, C57-C61) on performance metrics. OpenEval evaluation is SUPPORTED, praising quantitative metrics and acknowledged limitations; peer evaluation is SUPPORTED, accepting ~70% detection rate without direct challenge, though suggesting comparisons with LiDAR-based methods.

Partial overlap (C57-C59) on evaluation methodology. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes clear evaluation methodology; peer reviewers accepted these methodological definitions without challenge.

Overlap (C31-C32, C61, C86-C87) on model biases and limitations. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval praises honest assessment of systematic behaviors; peer reviewers accepted acknowledged limitations and inherent ambiguity in crown delineation.

Overlap (C35-C36, C70, C74-C75) on allometric relationships and ecological applications. OpenEval evaluation is SUPPORTED, noting patterns consistent with ecological expectations; peer evaluation is UNCERTAIN, requesting more concrete discussion of why density is important and how biodiversity could be assessed.

Substantial overlap (C65-C73) on applications. OpenEval evaluation is SUPPORTED, noting well-motivated applications with citations; peer evaluation is UNCERTAIN, explicitly requesting 'more concrete suggestions what could be done with the data' and specific discussion of density importance and biodiversity assessment.

Overlap (C76-C81) on cross-site analysis utility. OpenEval evaluation is SUPPORTED, accepting logical arguments as reasonable inferences; peer evaluation is UNCERTAIN, part of broader request for more concrete applications discussion.

Substantial overlap (C82-C84, C89-C90) on future research directions. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes appropriate framing as speculative with relevant citations; peer reviewers requested clarity on what would be needed for future LiDAR improvements but accepted these as reasonable goals.

Partial overlap (C85, C88) on validation recommendations. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval accepts framing as recommendations; peer reviewers did not challenge this framing, accepting manuscript despite acknowledged limitations.

Overlap (C100-C102) on dataset as living resource. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval praises balanced assessment of limitations and value; peer reviewers implicitly accepted this framing by accepting the manuscript.

OpenEval evaluated background context claims (C1-C2, C54) as SUPPORTED, noting they represent established knowledge from prior work. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims.
